today_summary: GCM26 at $4,186.6 with ATM IV 21.66% — a $57 (1.36%) 1σ daily move. The chain is ceiling-heavy: 120,153 call OI sits above spot against 28,096 put OI, and the $4,500/$4,510 pair alone stacks 16,738 calls (948 contracts traded today, the most active strike on the board). Nearest real floor is the $4,000 put stack at 4,633 OI with 661 lots traded. Max pain prints $5,500 but sits +$1,313 (+31%) above spot on legacy OI — treat it as noise, not a magnet.
five_day_thesis: Five sessions ago spot was $4,297.9; it is now $4,186.6, a -$111.3 (-2.59%) net loss, but the path is what matters: the entire decline came in one -$152.7 (-3.53%) break on 2026-09-29, and the last three sessions have ground higher in a tight $18.3 drift ($4,168.3 → $4,179.6 → $4,186.6). Windowed net GEX has halved from +370.6 to +178.0 (-52%), and the near-spot picture is worse than that headline: net GEX within ±$200 of spot is -223.5, with cumulative GEX running negative from the bottom of the chain all the way to the $4,800 flip strike — spot is sitting deep in dealer short gamma, which is exactly why 09-29 gapped the way it did. The structural change this week is the call wall collapsing from $6,000 to $5,500 (-$500) on 2026-10-01 after holding $6,000 for four straight sessions — upside supply has been pulled sharply lower. The $3,500 put wall has not moved once in five days (6,061 OI), and max pain has been frozen at $5,500 across all five, so neither is giving a directional signal. ATM IV spiked to 22.03% on the break and has only bled back to 21.66% (+0.58pp over the window), leaving premium still bid relative to the $4,100–$4,300 range price is actually respecting.

prediction: Neutral, range-bound $4,100–$4,300 until one side breaks. The $4,500/$4,510 call stack (16,738 OI) caps rallies and the $4,000 put stack (4,633 OI) floors dips, but short gamma below the $4,800 flip means whichever edge fails will overshoot rather than mean-revert. A close under $4,000 reopens the slide toward the untouched $3,500 put wall; a sustained bid through $4,300 puts the $4,400–$4,500 supply shelf in play.
